newsitem.title: CHINA: China huge opportunity for firms - Australian PM.
newsitem.headline: China huge opportunity for firms - Australian PM.

text.p: China's rapid economic growth presented Australian firms with a huge opportunity, Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Sunday, adding that he aimed to boost bilateral commercial ties to a new level.

Howard, visiting China's financial centre at the start of a four-day visit to China, attended a contract signing by an Australian company Sigtec for the provision of a computer taxi booking system to a Shanghai taxi firm.
"What we've just seen is a good example that you don't have to be (major Australian firm) BHP to succeed in China," Howard told reporters after the signing.
"It's another illustration that lively, innovative and expansionist small businesses can also do very well in a big market such as China," he added.
He later told a business lunch that when he meets Chinese leaders in Beijing on Monday he would be mainly aiming to boost commercial ties.

"I want to discuss with (Chinese leaders) how our economic cooperation might be lifted to a new level," he said. "In doing so we need to build on the trust and knowledge that our respective business communities have built up over the years."

"The growth and increased openness of the Chinese economy present enormous opportunities for Australians," Howard added, pointing out that in recent years Australian exports to China had grown twice as fast as the country's overall exports.
He said he also wanted to encourage China to invest more in Australia, already one of the top destinations for Chinese investment funds.
Howard, who arrived in Shanghai on Friday, was due to travel on Beijing on Sunday evening.
